name: Tom mu ni
summary: Clawless slipper lobster, boiled until tender, with white tail meat somewhere between shrimp and lobster and sweeter than other lobster. Dip it in lime, salt, and Phú Quốc pepper.
origin: Phu Quoc, on the specialty-seafood account.
texture: White meat. The specialty-seafood account says the texture sits between shrimp and lobster.
taste: Sweeter than other lobster, on that account. The dip is lime, salt, and Phú Quốc pepper. The meat is boiled until tender and aromatic.
howToEat: Crack the tail and dip the meat in lime, salt, and pepper.
where: Upmarket seafood restaurants and the night market.
seoTitle: Tom mu ni — slipper lobster on Phu Quoc
seoDescription: Tôm mũ ni is boiled slipper lobster with sweet white tail meat, dipped in lime, salt, and Phú Quốc pepper.
